notes.meaning: The Lord brings ruin and disorder to the land, turning its surface upside down and scattering the people who live there. After warning nearby nations, the prophet announces God's judgment reaching across the whole land and the wider world. No human power can stop the Lord when He decides to empty the land of its pride.

God's judgment treats everyone the exact same way, no matter their rank, wealth, or job. Priests suffer just like regular worshippers, masters like servants, and lenders like borrowers. Earthly status and money cannot buy protection when God calls people to account.

differ.view: Some believe God will take faithful believers to heaven in a rapture before this total judgment begins, sparing them from experiencing this destruction on earth.

notes.meaning: The land will be stripped bare and emptied of its treasures and inhabitants. This ruin is completely certain because the Lord Himself has spoken it. Human promises often fail, but God's warnings always come to pass.

The land and the world dry up and wither away like fading plants. Even the proud rulers and noble people waste away under God's hand. Creation itself suffers distress because of the rebellion of human beings.

The people have polluted the earth through their wickedness, breaking God's moral laws and ignoring His commands. They have violated the lasting covenant of life and order that God established. Sin does not hurt only the sinner; it brings corruption upon the whole surrounding creation.

A divine curse consumes the land, leaving its inhabitants to bear the guilt of their actions. The people are burned up under God's fierce anger, leaving only a tiny remnant alive. Hope ultimately rests only on God's mercy to spare and redeem.

The sweet wine dries up, and the grapevines wither away in the fields. People who once loved parties and feasts are left groaning in sadness. When God takes away basic harvests, worldly pleasures quickly vanish.

The happy beat of tambourines stops, and the lively strumming of harps goes silent. The noisy cheering of partygoers is brought to an end. All careless revelry fades away when God visits a nation in judgment.

People no longer sit together singing songs while drinking wine. Any strong drink left behind tastes bitter because grief and fear spoil every earthly taste. Trouble and distress turn former luxuries into sour reminders of loss.

The city is shattered and falls into total confusion and chaos. The houses are blocked up and shut tight so that nobody can go inside. Disorder ruins human security when God breaks down ungodly cities.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some scholars view this shattered city specifically as Jerusalem falling to Babylon in 587 BC rather than a general symbol of human pride.

notes.meaning: People cry out in the streets because the wine has run out and their parties are over. Gladness disappears like the fading light of sunset, and celebration is driven from the land. Earthly pleasures cannot bring lasting joy when trouble strikes.

The city is left in complete desolation, stripped of its life and beauty. Its strong city gates, which used to be the center of civic life and protection, are smashed into rubble. Pride in human defenses cannot stand against the judgment of God.

Across the earth and among the nations, only a tiny remnant of people will survive. They will be like the few stray olives left high in the tree after the harvest, or the few grapes left on the vine. God always preserves a small, faithful people even in times of wide destruction.

The surviving remnant lifts up its voice to shout with joy and thankfulness. From the western seas, they celebrate the majesty and goodness of the Lord who saved them. Even amid deep ruin, God's people find reasons to praise His power and mercy.

The faithful survivors call on one another to praise the Lord from every corner of the earth. Whether in the east or on distant islands in the west, believers give honor to the God of Israel. True faith brings praise to God even when believers are scattered in foreign lands.

Songs praising the Righteous One rise up from the farthest edges of the earth. Yet the prophet cries out in grief because evil and deceit still run rampant around him. God's servants can rejoice in His future victory while still mourning the persistent treachery of this world.

Terrors, pits, and traps await the people living on the earth. Like wild animals driven by hunters, sinners face one danger right after another. Running away from God's judgment only leads into another trap.

Anyone who runs from the noise of panic falls straight into a pit, and anyone climbing out gets caught in a snare. The floodgates of heaven open and the earth shakes at its foundations, reminding readers of Noah's flood. God's universal judgment leaves no escape route for unrepentant sinners.

The earth breaks apart, splits open, and shakes with great violence. God rocks the world to show that no created thing is permanent or self-sufficient. This severe shaking warns all nations that creation belongs entirely to its Maker.

The earth stumbles like a drunkard and sways like a flimsy watchman's hut in the wind. The heavy weight of human sin crushes it down so that it collapses and cannot get back up. Sin is a crushing burden that ruins the physical creation until God renews it.

On that coming day, the Lord will bring judgment on both the powers in the heavenly realm and the kings ruling on the earth. Rebel spiritual forces and proud human rulers will both be held accountable before God. No ruler, whether visible or invisible, can match God's ultimate authority.

These rebel rulers and spiritual powers will be gathered together and locked away like prisoners in an underground dungeon. After many days, God will call them forward for their final reckoning. God limits the reach of evil and keeps all His enemies under His control until judgment day.

differ.view: Some hold that the confinement for many days refers to rebel powers and Satan being bound during a literal thousand-year reign of Christ before final judgment.

notes.meaning: The moon will look pale and the sun will seem embarrassed because the Lord of hosts will rule in glorious majesty on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem. His brilliant presence before His elders will outshine the brightest lights in the sky. When God sets up His glorious kingdom, all human and created glory fades into shadow.

differ.view: The reign of the Lord on Mount Zion will be a literal earthly government centered in the physical city of Jerusalem during the millennium.
The reign in Zion and Jerusalem describes the spiritual gathering and restoration of Christ's church, rather than a political throne in earthly Jerusalem.
